_notes.about: Lesson 10 in English (en and en-GB, which has its own keyboard). From the lesson plan "Typing Game Sentence Bank: Lessons 2-13". The id is the lesson's scoreboard: never change it.
_notes.intro: Page 1, before the keys: anything that doesn't fit on Page 2 (lesson 1: "what is touch typing?"). Leave it out and the lesson starts at the new keys. "title" and "paragraphs"; in a paragraph, **bold** and [E] (a key drawn as a key: [space], [;], [Tab] ...). "picture": "hands" (the default: the hands over the lesson's keyboard), "none", or a picture file in images/ (with "pictureAlt", what it shows). With "hands": "reach" sends fingers to keys ({"lm": "e", "rm": "i"}: lp lr lm li, rp rr rm ri; keys "e", ";", "ShiftL", "ShiftR" ...; the others stay home), and "keys" says which keys show: "letters" (the default), "shift", "symbols" or "all".
_notes.hideHand: "left", "right" or "none": that hand isn't drawn on Page 2, and its column of new keys isn't listed.
_notes.sentenceLists: Up to four lists: name (shown above the typing box, or ""), count (how many to pick at random each attempt; 0 = unused) and sentences. Use real words, and only keys taught so far. Lesson 1 has no end mark because ";" hasn't been taught. Write ⇥ for the Tab key and ↵ for Enter.

title: Lesson 10: B and N

intro.title: Index fingers down and in to B and N
paragraphs: [B] and [N] are on the bottom row, between your hands: down one row, and in towards the middle of the keyboard.
The left index finger reaches from [F] down and to the right to [B]. The right index finger reaches from [J] down and to the left to [N].
Now each index finger looks after six keys: [R] [F] [V] [T] [G] [B] on the left, and [U] [J] [M] [Y] [H] [N] on the right.

advice: [B] is down and to the right of [F], below [G]. Reach with your left index finger, press [B], and come back to [F].
[N] is down and to the left of [J], below [H]. Reach with your right index finger, press [N], and come back to [J].
Keep your other fingers on the home row while the index finger reaches.
